problem: Mobile robots in search and rescue, construction, and exploration operate with incomplete environment knowledge, under communication dropouts, limited compute and energy, and the need to work with humans; prior exploration and navigation methods handle these poorly.
motivation: Robots must act when teammates' intentions, unknown map regions, or human-provided guidance are unavailable or costly to exchange. Inferring intentions and environment structure can reduce communication bandwidth, extend exploration range, and enable intuitive human-robot interaction.
key_idea: Use learned inference of teammates' intentions and of unknown environment structure to drive robot decision making, culminating in zero-shot VLM-based navigation from human hand-drawn maps.
insight: Only the abstract is available, so no ablations can be cited. The abstract suggests that implicit intention prediction reduces redundant coverage without communication, and that predicting unseen map layout reduces the need for map exchange and extends exploration range.
method: MADE-Net: multi-agent deep RL with macro actions that predicts the tasks teammates will execute, to reduce redundant coverage under communication dropouts
4CNet: deep learning map-prediction framework that infers the layout of unknown areas in cluttered, rough-terrain environments, for coverage under energy and communication limits
HAM-Nav: zero-shot navigation framework combining intention and environment inference, using a VLM to interpret hand-drawn maps in various styles

setting.backbone: MADE-Net (multi-agent DRL), 4CNet (DL map predictor), HAM-Nav (VLM, zero-shot; model not specified in abstract)
setting.training_data: Not stated in abstract; HAM-Nav is zero-shot
setting.action_space: Not stated in abstract (macro actions for MADE-Net)
setting.simulator: Simulation plus real world (specific simulators not stated)

results: The abstract reports qualitative results only. MADE-Net reduces exploration time and local interactions and outperforms traditional and DRL benchmarks. 4CNet beats GAN and autoencoder baselines on map prediction accuracy and coverage. HAM-Nav achieves high success rates and user satisfaction in simulation and real-world tests.
limitations: Abstract gives no quantitative results or details on baselines and settings
HAM-Nav relies on a VLM interpreting hand-drawn maps, so it is likely sensitive to sketch quality and style
